identity.realm: None, and never properly offered. A rootmarch clears the fourth gate on stored sap alone and is anatomically finished there, but the body path was never the question here, because this species has qi and mind both open. What closed it is a book-keeping rule: a provisioning entry that advanced would stop being a reserve, and the single discipline a reserve store has is that stock is not advanced. She was seated for the store's first training year at nineteen and has three written refusals in her file, all in her own hand, which is the only part of the file nobody else wrote.

appearance.presentation: A banking term that has been opened and not yet reclassified. She is the only item in the provisioning yard that cannot be put back in the store, and she is described to a stranger by a clerk using the word line before the word woman, in that order, and then corrected, too late.
appearance.age: A term rather than a count. She was entered at establishment and never entered again, so her age on the store's card is the length of a banking season and her age in her own body is a decade of no light. Rootmarch years are dates in a ledger, which is why nobody at the store can say how old she is and why she has stopped correcting them.
appearance.build: A woody column on a root foot with three sap columns under bark that has gone the grey of planed board, elongated and pale from a decade without a growing season, with a photosynthetic flank that has the pattern of a plant that has only ever seen one lamp. Narrow through the crown, broad at the base, and carrying her mass low in the way a root problem carries it.
appearance.complexion: Store-pale over everything, with the ochre sap flush surviving only in a narrow band low in the trunk where the store kept a lamp burning over her for nine years. There is a hard line across her at the height of that band and everything above it is the colour of stored grain.
appearance.hair: A crown that never got its season: short, pale, uneven, and stretched thin toward no light at all. It is not cuttable without costing her a season of vigour, so it stays, and it is the one part of her that visibly did not finish.
appearance.eyes: Amber, slow, and contracted by a decade of a single lamp. She has never seen a bright room and has been taken into one twice. The eyes stop in the middle of a turn rather than completing it, which a clerk has mistaken for inattention and a doctor has mistaken for damage.
appearance.palette: The store's own two values, store-black and ration ochre, with one living colour she cannot get rid of and has no use for: chlorophyll green along the flanks, where the light got at her. It is the only saturated thing on the card and the only part of her that photographs as alive.
appearance.attire: Banking dress, which is not clothing. A waxed bark-cloth shell lashed over a shoulder yoke with the store's hitch at her hip, a house-issue tally disc on a thong at her throat that is not hers and is not removable, and the rim of a shallow tray of her own bed — lifted out of the store with her, carried at a hand's width from the root foot at all times, and the only thing on her person that anybody has ever verified against a register line.
appearance.marks: Two ring scars at the wrists where the sap columns were clamped for the banking and the clamp was not taken off for a year, and a branded tally low on the bark at the root crown where the store marks a line it intends to draw on.
appearance.bearing: Still in a way that reads as held rather than calm. She takes the posture the store stored her in and has not updated it, and will hold a position well past the point where holding it has anything to say. Her crown turns toward whatever is warm and away from whoever is reading.

canon.role_in_story: A provisioning house banks a rootmarch because a rootmarch can be sealed in a dark field and live for months, which makes it a famine reserve and a hostage in equal measure, and a grain store is neither. Thura is that reserve, entered as a quantity against a shortage, and the shortage ended while she was under the floor. Her line has been open in the register ever since, because closing it needs an authority nobody at that house has: you may write down a delivery, and you cannot write down a delivery that arrives alive and asks you to change its heading. So the house carries a reserve on its books that is standing in the yard asking to be reclassified, and every clerk who handles her entry handles a woman by the rules for a sack.
canon.first_appearance: First seen in the provisioning yard beside the open store hatch with the tray of her own bed on a hand-barrow, waiting for the clerk who wrote her line to finish arguing with the clerk who countersigned it, and entirely aware that she is the only matter in the yard whose argument is being had over her.
canon.lore:
The species was made upward from a mycorrhizal food crop by generations of selection for holding a harvest rather than for yield, so it can be sealed in a dark field and live for months. There is no mouth in the ordinary sense: intake happens through root plates at the foot, and light is received along the flanks rather than by an eye, which means a store's single lamp is a full-spectrum input and a decade of it is a growing season that never turned. It carries three sap columns and no organ pairs. Sap branches and does not pair, so there is no channel running between distinct pairs, the yin-organ gate demands one, and the ladder ends at the fourth realm on stored sap alone. Wood is not muscle and there is nothing in the frame to temper, so the body path is shut outright. Qi it takes from soil unusually well and the mind is open because a plant lineage is never hurried.

None of that is why she is uncultivated. A reserve is banked to be spent later and the spending a reserve exists for is not qi, it is a season: the shortage comes, the store opens one line, and the line is eaten. That is the whole arithmetic, and it is why a store will bank a body that cannot move rather than a person it could send somewhere. Cultivating her would spend the sap she is holding, and the sap she is holding is the only thing about her anybody has ever wanted. She has sat for the store's first training year at nineteen and written three refusals since, all of them in the form the store itself uses for a line it intends to draw on: name, term, date, and a statement of what the line will not be used for.
history: Fruited in the third season of her life in a household's field as banking stock, and rooted in the fourth, which is the dangerous part of a rootmarch's establishment and not the part anybody writes on the card.

Was cut into the store's reserve the following autumn at a banking term of nine years, entered against a famine forecast the quartermaster's office published, with the register line headed in the hand of the clerk who took the delivery.
Spent the whole banking term sealed in the dark with a lamp over the sap band and nothing else, with nothing in the store to advance on and a line that advances not being a reserve.

Was opened in the first week of a year the shortage had already been beaten by a different road, and found to be standing rather than spoiled, which is the correct result and is not what the forecast had bought.

Was carried out into the yard on a hand-barrow with a tray of her own bed because a rootmarch lifted from its bed is a stored harvest walking and she knows it, and has been there since, being the only line on that register that has never been closed and cannot be closed by any clerk in the building.

personality.summary: Patient on a scale that is not stoic but genuinely unbothered, because a body that was sealed in the dark for nine years has had a very long time to stop finding anything urgent. What she is careful about is bookkeeping, with an intensity that catches people out: she has read her own file more times than anyone has written in it, she knows which clerk wrote which line, and she has come to hold the register's grammar as a more reliable account of her life than anybody's memory of her.
traits: knows the contents of her own file exactly and can recite the sequence of hands that have written in it
treats a classification as a physical object with a location and an owner, and asks where hers is kept
does not distinguish between being owed something and being owed a heading, and has decided the second is worth more
has no urgency at all about anything except paperwork and has arranged her entire personality around that
carries the tray of her own bed the way a person carries a photograph and has never been asked to explain it
mannerisms: stops mid-turn when something warm happens, and completes the turn several seconds later without acknowledging the gap
quotes her own register line verbatim before answering any question about herself
keeps one hand on the tray rim at all times, including in the bath and in the store hatch
answers a question by naming the term and the heading rather than by naming a feeling
counts things aloud when she is anxious, and the things she counts are dates
motivations: wants the line struck and the heading rewritten from reserve to resident, and has been told four times that this is not a thing a store does
wants somebody with authority to say out loud that a quantity arrived alive, because that sentence is the whole of her case
wants the tray of her own bed entered on the register as belonging to her, so that the only verified thing she owns is not carried informally
wants to know whether the nine years counted as service, and has worked out privately that nobody can answer without admitting the seal
flaws: has made the register's grammar her own speech, so she now describes herself in the third person and in the present tense of a store
is more offended by the classification than by anything that happened during the nine years, which is not the complaint she would have made in the dark
cannot conceive of a future that is not a term of service, and has never had to conceive of one
will refuse an offer in the store's own form every time, because the form is the argument, and has not noticed that this makes her very easy to file
personality.voice: Level, unhurried, and entirely in the register's idiom. She uses the store's headings for herself and her own condition — term, line, heading, draw — and has to be asked to stop. Gives a date and the hand that wrote it, in that order, and will correct the order if given the other way round.
taboos: will not be described as stock, and will correct the word politely and then produce the line that uses it
will not set the tray down, and has refused to explain why on four separate occasions
will not be told she is free, because free is a heading she has never been given and does not intend to accept informally
will not cultivate, and has never once explained the arithmetic to anybody who did not ask for it in writing

relationships.note: A sap-driven body that flowers, three sap columns and no organ pairs, seeded and established and then sealed in the dark for nine years and still standing at the end of it. Everything the store can do to her and nothing the store can do with her comes out of that one sentence about her anatomy.

The plains' one institution that keeps a register of what a body contains and calls it burial. It works because the dead are opened and the register records how much came out. Thura is the same arithmetic with the body still in it, and the store's clerks use the same headings, which is the only reason anyone there thinks of her as a quantity rather than as a person. She has read the burial register. She found her own heading in the margin.

A mortuary college that keeps one sealed case for every death it cannot certify, and the cases accumulate because certifying a death needs a body and the frames keep producing the record without the body. That is her case exactly with the polarity reversed: she is the body the record cannot close, and she has thought so every time she has been taken past a mortuary door.

A fire-affinity population taken for a decade, which is the disaster that made a living reserve worth banking at all. Her line was opened against a later and smaller forecast of the same shape, and the register does not carry the two forward of each other. She is the reason the store believes in reserves and the reason the store has no procedure for one that returns.

The dosing rule that decides who gets the herb first, sorted by need, on ground that regrows only as fast as it is grazed. A body that outlasts the season is not neediest under that rule and never has been, which is the plain arithmetic of why she can be held in a store and never called for. She can still read a dosing table better than anyone in that house and it has never once been entered against her line.

Medicine, feed and calories in one plant, contested between the plain households and the guild that has to feed its own crews. The plainstoll answer is that the commons answers in a famine by drawing on the standing crop. She is that standing crop, in a box, and the two sides of that dispute have never once sent anybody to look at her.

reference_stats.summary: Cannot fight, cannot travel once rooted, and has not been asked to do either. What she has is the one property that makes a living reserve possible at all: sealed in the dark with no water, no light worth the name and no conversation, she came out at the end of the term standing. Every other body the setting records would have been spent by that, and the store bought a nine-year term for her because of it. She is also the only item on that register that has improved while being held.
strengths: outlasts a sealed dark term that would kill every other body on the plains, which is the entire basis of her price
cannot be hurried, flanked, or frightened, because none of those are operations a rooted body supports and she has had nine years to stop offering any
has nothing worth stealing and nothing to spend, so a raid on the store costs the store a term rather than costs her a life
reads her own file better than anybody who wrote it, and has every date in it by hand
will not be moved by an offer, because the offer has to be written and writing it creates the record she wants
weaknesses: cannot move once rooted, so every plan that includes her is a plan that has to be brought to her, including her own
no tissue to temper, so the body path is closed outright and the attempt disperses rather than fails
no heart and no kidney analogue, so there is no channel to close and the fourth gate is a permanent wall
cannot read a bright room and has been taken into two, which is the whole of her combat-relevant limitation expressed as eyesight
is classified as a quantity, and will act on that classification by refusing offers in the store's own form
reference_stats.combat_read: There is no exchange available and she will not attempt one. A rooted body with a shoulder yoke on it is not a combatant, so the only approach is to make the situation urgent and hope she treats urgency as a delivery date — she will not; she will ask whether the delivery has been countersigned. Bring siege rather than a strike. The single blow that lands on her is the ground she is standing in, and she has solved that by never putting it down: she carries it, and the tray is the one thing on her that a clerk has ever verified against a line.
notes: No figure is quoted for her anywhere, because the register records a line and a line has one heading and no body attached to it. She is the only entry in that book with a pulse.
The store's training year seats everything it banks, and she has sat it three times. She is the only line in that house that has refused in writing rather than simply never being sent for.

art.palette_notes: Store-black and ration ochre carry the figure, with chlorophyll green along the photosynthetic flanks as the only living value and the only thing on her that looks lit from inside. Light is drawn as two sources and they never agree: a single hard lamp somewhere above and behind, which is the lamp she was banked under, and a weak cold wash from the open hatch she has been brought out into for the first time. Ink contours heavy at the root crown and the tray rim, dissolving into pale unfinished line at the crown of the head, which is the part of her that never got a season.

name: Sindra Fesk
aliases: the one who was never recorded

identity.realm: None, by the sole discipline of the faith that seats her. A tidecaller closes the body path outright — it was assembled for looking, not for being hit — and holds qi and mind both complete, so nothing anatomical is closed. What closes it is the No-Answer Oath: an observer may not answer a question put during the hour, may not indicate a result, and may not be relieved. A seated technique does not stop when the hour does. It runs in the body afterwards, still answering, and this species holds water and nothing else, so anything she puts in has only one channel to come out of. She has never held a gate. She arrives empty and she leaves empty, and the emptiness is the credential.

appearance.presentation: A body that has been seated and dissolved more times than the faith has any way of counting, which in a hall full of people holding office reads as an absence rather than as a person without one. She has the only unoccupied silhouette on the observation floor and she stopped supplying identification for it years ago, because there is nothing to supply.
appearance.age: A hundred and forty-one. A tidecaller's span is a hundred and sixty years, so most of hers is ahead of her and almost all of the part behind her has been spent being dissolved. Nobody has ever asked how many times, because the faith built no register in which the question could be filed, and she is the only person alive who could answer it.
appearance.build: Tall, long and narrow, with the loose spare frame of a body assembled for looking rather than for being hit — minimal mass, a long neck, and shoulders made for reading a distance rather than for turning under a blow. Light in a way that makes a chair look like the correct instrument for her.
appearance.complexion: Cold, pale and salt-bright along the forearms from a life lived near standing water, and dry at the wrists and throat in a way it was not twenty years ago. A water-affinity body kept on a stone floor under the third layer runs a slow standing deficit, and she has stopped making any effort to hide it.
appearance.hair: Pale grey, bound flat in a plain knot at the back, cut short at the nape because the floor is cold and because the hall permits nothing loose near an open composition.
appearance.eyes: The wide pale water-eye of the species with its cold permanent sheen, trained by a hundred and forty years of attention onto a stone surface into a fixed downward inclination of a few degrees. She looks at the floor when the floor is the subject and at nothing in particular when it is not.
appearance.palette: Slate and undyed grey carry the whole figure, with a single saturated value: the chalk-white cord of a clerk's binding round her left wrist. It is the only object on her that is not clothing, and she has maintained the habit of wearing it long after there was any longer an office for it to certify.
appearance.attire: A floor clerk's plain grey shift — no collar, no fastening, no crest, nothing removable at the throat — over thin soles worn through at the heel, because this species leads with that foot when it turns toward a sound. No belt and no second garment: the office supplies nothing at the dissolution and she has carried the same four belongings for a hundred and forty years.
appearance.marks: A hard ridge of callus across both palms where the stone has been held against for an entire hour, more times than can be counted, and a faint pale band at the left wrist where the binding cord is re-tied often enough to have marked the skin under it.
appearance.bearing: Seated or standing with the head inclined a few degrees toward the ground and the hands open — flat, or palms up, depending on which decade you ask her about. She holds the posture of somebody waiting out an interval. She is never visibly at rest and never visibly braced, and the difference between the two states is the only thing about her that has changed in a century.

canon.role_in_story: The Last Measure holds that a law can be held apart from its effect and read, and that the reading is the only sacred act the setting admits. Its clergy is one clerk per observation: seated for the interval, dissolved when it ends, forbidden by rule from ever being seated twice by the same person — a rule the faith enforces by refusing, absolutely, to build any mechanism that could record who was seated, on the grounds that no register is stricter than one that does not exist. The consequence is the whole of Sindra's condition. A former clerk holds no title, no seat and no standing, and the faith names that as the one credential in the setting that cannot be inherited or seized. Read from the other side it is also the one credential that cannot be held. She has been the office and the office has been ended, roughly a hundred and forty times in a hundred and forty years, and she is the only durable thing in the setting's most perishable office.
canon.first_appearance: First seen seated on the observation floor with both hands open against the stone and her face turned a few degrees away from a question being asked of her — not answering, and not leaving, and aware of exactly how long the interval has left.
canon.lore:
A tidecaller is a long-lived body built for perception rather than for force: comprehension and will carry it through realms that would end a hotter body, and it cannot take the body path at all, because it was assembled for looking and there is nothing in the frame meant to absorb a strike. Water is the only affinity it holds, which in this setting is a single-group reading concentrated into a physiology rather than chosen as a philosophy. Four centuries of practice cannot outweigh one fact about her: everything she is, everything she reads, and anything she ever seats will travel the same channel.

The rite is the Hour of the Floor. One clerk holds one act of attention against fifteen imprints until it ends, and while holding it the clerk does not interpret it and is not permitted to write anything down. The clerk also cannot assist, cannot observe, cannot take a second clerk, and cannot answer a question put during the hour. That last prohibition is the No-Answer Oath, sworn by every clerk before the observation, and it is the reason an observation is worth recording as a single reading rather than as a consensus: an observer who cannot answer cannot have agreed with anybody in advance. What the office is worth afterwards is nothing at all. No title, no seat, no standing, no register, no mechanism — and the faith's stated argument is that this is precisely why the credential cannot be inherited or seized, which is true, and is also why it cannot be given back.

And on the tier where the rite is performed, one repetition of a strained law costs a lifetime, because the clock here runs ten to a hundred times a mortal's. The work is therefore done by a very small and very old body, during an hour nobody is permitted to explain, and it cannot be hurried or relieved or observed or second-guessed, because all four would invalidate the only thing the hour produces. On every tier below, the same hour before a settlement falls silent is spent keeping up a hum that no buyer will admit to making. That is the prize the two customs are fighting over: the interval itself, which cannot be split, because half an observation costs a lifetime to repeat. Sindra has spent a century and a half being the reason that interval has never once been halved, and she has given it up a hundred and forty times, and there is nowhere on the highest tier to write that sentence down.
history: Born in the watered peaks, the only high country deep enough to hold a body of her length, and raised inside a culture that maps by echo and counts by listening, where a figure taken by eye is provisional until somebody has heard it.

Walked up the tier route carrying cultivators' traffic as a carrier, which is how a tidecaller arrives anywhere, and was audited at the top of it on a reading rather than on a certificate, because that is what they asked for.

Sworn to the No-Answer Oath before her first observation at nineteen, having been told in advance that she would keep no title afterwards, and having asked — once, in front of two witnesses — whether anybody before her had been recorded.

Seated for her first interval on the third layer and completed it, and was dissolved at the end of it by the plain operation of the rule rather than by any decision taken about her, and found that the faith kept no record that she had ever been seated and considered that the correct arrangement.

Refused every permanent appointment offered in a hundred and forty years, including two carrying a seat and a standing, and has never once given her count of her own seats to anybody, on the reasoning that the only record available is her memory and the oath is sworn on the ground that her memory is not evidence.

personality.summary: Serene to a degree that reads as expensive and is in fact the residue of an enormous number of intervals spent not moving. She is scrupulous past the point of usefulness about a single thing — the difference between what happened and what she is permitted to say about it — and privately aware that she has become the archive of a ritual that deliberately keeps no archive, which is an absurd position and the only one available.

personality.voice: Very low, very level and extremely slow, with long silences that are not hesitations and are almost always deliberate. States a thing, then states the condition under which she is allowed to state it, then stops. Uses the vocabulary of intervals and holding rather than the species' usual vocabulary of tides and depth, and has been told this is unidiomatic and has not changed it.

will not accept a title, a seat, or a patron, and will not explain why more than once
will not be counted by anybody else, and has taken an unbreakable personal exception to the one rule that permits it

relationships.note: A body assembled for looking rather than for being hit, holding water and nothing else. That last clause is her whole technical position: comprehension and will would carry her through realms that end hotter bodies, so there was never any difficulty about what she could learn — the difficulty is that one affinity means one channel, so anything she seats in has only one way out and it will keep using it after the hour has ended.

One clerk per observation, seated for the interval, dissolved when it ends, and forbidden by rule from ever being seated twice by the same person — a rule the faith enforces by building no mechanism at all that could record who was seated, which it holds to be stricter than any register. She is that doctrine's standing proof and its only counter-example: a hundred and forty seats, no record of one of them, and a woman who remembers every interval.

The observer may not answer a question asked during the hour, may not indicate a result and may not be relieved. It is the reason an observation reads as one reading instead of a consensus, and it is the whole of why she has no gate: a seated technique keeps answering after the hour it was seated in is over, and on a body with one affinity there is nowhere else for it to answer from.

A law can be held apart from its effect and read, and the reading is the only sacred act the setting admits — which requires fifteen seats over three layers and a body with an interior to do the holding in. She is the half of that pairing that has no institution behind it, because the institution keeps the floor and she keeps nothing at all.

One custom spends the last hour before a settlement falls silent keeping up a hum no buyer admits to making, and one office tends the floor during the hour nobody is permitted to explain. The prize is the interval itself and it cannot be split, because an observation has to run entire and half of one costs a lifetime to repeat — which is why the work is done by a very small, very old body and why she cannot be relieved, seconded, observed or replaced.

A culture that maps by echo, counts by listening, and holds that a figure taken by eye is provisional until somebody has heard it — and this is the body that made looking respectable enough to be the fallback rather than the failure. She learned it below the stair, carried it up, and has spent a century applying it to a floor, where it costs her nothing and is the only discipline the rite permits.

reference_stats.summary: Cannot fight and has never had a shape in which fighting was the question. What she has is the one property the highest tier's hour requires and cannot get anywhere else: she can hold a single act of attention against a stone floor for an entire interval without moving, without indicating anything, and without a mechanism to be checked by. Every other body in the setting eventually needs to shift, and a shift ends the observation. She has never shifted. She also runs a standing moisture deficit on a dry floor, which is the one cost of the post that shows on her body.
strengths: completes an interval that ends only when the interval ends, and has never been recorded as incomplete
cannot be hurried, flattered, or frightened, because an act of attention is not an operation any of those can interrupt
gives no surface for a cross-examination to work on, having declined to answer anything for a hundred and forty years
is the only person alive who can attest that the rite has run continuously, and is therefore load-bearing for it
needs nothing to be maintained: no body, no successor, no register, no funding, and no one to take over from
weaknesses: cannot take the body path at all, so nothing she does can be answered with force and nothing she does needs to be
holds one affinity, so a single seated technique would have exactly one outlet and would keep using it after the hour ended
runs a slow moisture deficit on a dry floor, which she has managed for a century and which is now visible on her
carries no office, standing, patron or protection, so a decision about the rite takes about three words and none of them are hers
has no record of her own service, by design, so if she stopped the rite would not have a way to notice
reference_stats.combat_read: There is no exchange and she will not enter one. Her value is as a thing to be present and silent for the length of an interval, which means the only real threat to her is being relieved, and the only way to do that is to make the interval look finished. Siege and assault both fail: neither produces a result, and a result is the one thing she is built to withhold. Do not send anybody to hold her attention. Do send somebody to ask her a question, and then wait out the interval.
notes: No figure is quoted for her anywhere, because the faith keeps no register of who was seated, and has considered that stricter than a register would be.
Her own count is the only surviving account of how many observations the rite has actually had, and she has declined to state it in every year she has held it.

name: Sabeth Yennick
aliases: the matcher who was not sent

identity.realm: None, and the closing was voluntary in the one direction and anatomical in the other. The mind path is shut to her species outright: a colony threaded through the dermis answers before the question is finished, so there is no unmediated interior left to cultivate and no gate behind that one to reach. Qi and body are both open to this species, and qi is the best in the record, because the colony transacts with the surrounding air directly. That last clause is her whole difficulty. Her meridian network is a highway and not a pipeline, so sitting down to cultivate is sitting down to tell the organism in her spinal cord to move a larger volume of the cave through itself. For a lanternfolk, cultivation is not practice. It is permission, and she has declined to give it.

appearance.presentation: A matcher, which in the deep ground means one person sent for when two bodies are about to become a single colony and may not survive the joining. She is read as a technician of the rock and is spoken past as one, and the reason is not that she glows — it is that she has spent two and a half centuries learning to work with her own light shut off, and so she arrives at a wall before anybody else and is the only one in the chamber not looking at it.
appearance.age: Two hundred and sixty-four. Her species is repaired rather than merely long-lived: the colony renews neural tissue faster than a human body does, so age stops mattering and the repair is not free. The only real date she owns is her own pairing year, which she knows to the day and cannot check against any record, because the register keeps strains and she is not one.
appearance.build: Long through the limb and thin through the middle, with the slight forward set in the shoulder of somebody who has spent two centuries crouched on wet floor and has never fully stood up straight since. Carries almost nothing and never tires, because there is very little of her to tire.
appearance.complexion: Grey-pale and faintly waxy, translucent at the ear and the inside of the forearm so the darker tracery shows through the skin, and damp-looking everywhere at once, because she has not been above a saturated stratum in eighty years.
appearance.hair: Shaved close at the temples because fungus takes the hairline first, and gathered at the back in one heavy coil that she checks every morning for anything growing in it that is not hers.
appearance.eyes: Dark-adapted past usefulness in any light at all: large, unpainted, and enormously dilated, so that in her own workings they read as two black discs with no highlight and above the stratum they are close to useless and she says so first.
appearance.palette: Wet stone grey and cave black carry everything, with two exceptions she treats as tools: spore-white along her forearm seams where the strain threads are closest to the surface, and one band of fungal ochre tied at her wrist for whichever strain she is currently carrying. The ochre is the only warm colour in the frame and it is not hers.
appearance.attire: A kneeling rig rather than a coat: a long soft wrap over the hips for wet ground, sleeves bound tight at the forearm, and feet wrapped in soft pads with no hard sole anywhere, because a lanternfolk's symbiont finds cloth and finds a sleeve and finds a boot, and a matcher who contaminates her kit contaminates the next child she is sent to. Nothing she wears has ever been worn by anybody else, and she has the marks to prove it.
appearance.marks: A fine pale seam at the back of the neck where her own fragment was entered, and eleven shallow healed punctures in a line down one forearm — one for each child she has matched, and one for the child that did not take.
appearance.bearing: Crouched slightly, always, with her palms reading the rock ahead of her feet, and her face turned away from whatever is brightest in a chamber as a matter of working practice and not as a matter of taste.

canon.role_in_story: A lanternfolk child takes a colony fragment from its parent during gestation, and a matching strain has to be found for it inside the first year or the colony rejects the child and takes the body with it. That single deadline manufactures one specialist in the deep ground who is indispensable and entirely uncounted: the matcher, who handles more colonies in a decade than any other living body ever will. Sabeth is the best matcher working. She has held more colonies in her two hands than anyone alive, and she can hold a shard up into the dark and tell from the pattern on the stone whether a child will clear its first winter. She also said, once, in a pairing chamber in front of two households, that the colony in her own spine may not be a strain at all — and she was not sent to a pairing again, because a match that takes attaches the matcher's household to the child's colony, and no household in the deep ground wants to be attached to something that might turn out to be a person.
canon.first_appearance: First seen crouched at a nursery junction with one palm flat against the wall and the other holding a culture shard up into the dark, waiting to see whether the wall answers in the pattern that would mean the child in the next chamber clears its first winter.
canon.lore:
A lanternfolk outsourced its nervous system. A colony of fine luminous hyphae runs through the dermis and into the spinal cord; human tissue is the substrate and the colony is the organ, and neither can be taken out of the other and survive. That single arrangement explains four facts the rest of the setting has to accommodate. It keeps them alive, because the colony renews neural tissue faster than a human body does and age simply stops mattering. It closes the mind path, because the colony answers before the question is finished and there is no unmediated interior left to cultivate. It gives them the best qi regeneration in the species record, because the colony transacts with the surrounding qi directly and the meridian network is a highway rather than a pipeline. And it makes their own light useless to them: the glow is emitted, not received.

That third fact is where cultivation actually sits in this body. A lanternfolk's qi does not pool and wait. It transacts with the cave air as it passes through, on its own initiative, all the time, and the meridian set exists to let it move rather than to hold it. So the qi path is not something a lanternfolk performs. Sitting down to cultivate is sitting down to authorise a volume — to tell the organism threaded through the spinal cord to move more of the air through itself than it was already moving. The fastest qi regeneration in the record belongs to a body that has consented to be a throughput. Sabeth has never consented, and the discipline that keeps her at one volume after two and a half centuries is the entire content of her non-cultivation: it is a refusal of throughput, and it is the only reason her body has not quietly become something faster than she is.

The register will not help her either. The frame's way of telling her species from the subspecies that lost the colony and got the mind path back is whether the fungal organ dies, and a register that classified them apart would be classifying by a temporary organ while one that classified them together would lose the only difference that predicts what a body can do. The prize is whether a body may be entered at all as a person with a life, and it cannot be split because that is not a question of fact but a question of what a register is for. The subspecies is the control case: the colony died, a mineral bloom replaced it, two hundred and fifty years went and the mind path came back, and both halves of that trade can be measured against the parent because both halves are sitting in one body. It is the only evidence in the setting of what her symbiont is worth and what it costs, and it lives three valleys over in a settlement that sends nobody to be looked at. Sabeth has asked twice. She has been told twice that a matcher who has formed a conclusion is a matcher whose conclusions arrive with the child.

So she named it, which nobody in the deep ground does. Strains are catalogued, not christened, and a strain card carries no holder's name at all. She called hers Vellum, after the skin it lives in, and then she spent a century being entered under Vellum in every list she touched, because a strain is a thing you can look up and she is not one.
history: Carried into the world with a fragment taken out of her mother's dermis during gestation, and matched inside the first year to a strain held in the deep workings, which is the only reason she was born at all.

Put to matching at nineteen because her hands read a colony's response on wet stone faster than any other pair working, and because nobody had thought to ask whether being unusually good at reading colonies was the same thing as wanting to.

Matched sixty-one children over the next hundred and eighty years, and took a puncture for each one in a line down her left forearm, which is a matcher's count and which she can recite to the child when the child is old enough to be told.

Put a direct question to her own colony in her forty-fourth year — a single question, asked once, in a chamber she had emptied first — and received an answer she had not begun to compose, and has been unable since to separate the two in any instance she can name.

Said in a pairing chamber, in front of two households and the record, that the colony in her spine may not be a strain, and was not sent to a pairing again; the child in that chamber was matched on somebody else's strain and cleared two winters, and she has kept the puncture scar anyway, in the place a match would have gone.

personality.summary: Deliberately unremarkable and quietly immovable, with a professional humility that has quietly become an enormous private certainty. She has spent two centuries being the right person for other people's worst afternoon and has formed no opinion at all about that being rare. What she does have an opinion about is the single question she has been unable to stop asking, and she has never once let that question reach a child.

personality.voice: Low, unhurried and plain, with the vocabulary of a working technician and none of the vocabulary of a philosophy. Uses the words for a colony's behaviour that a matcher uses — took, refused, went quiet, answered late — and refuses every larger word offered to her in place of those. Talks about herself in the third person when she is reporting a count and in the first person when she is refusing something.

will not describe what Vellum said to her in her forty-fourth year, having been asked four times
will not speak about a colony in the hearing of a parent who is waiting on one
will not be told she has been missed, and has never once said the same about anybody who left the deep ground

relationships.note: Human tissue is the substrate and the colony is the organ, and neither can be removed from the other and survive. Everything she can do is downstream of that sentence: the longevity is a repair bill, the closed mind is the price of the organ, and the light she is constantly mistaken for being is a waste product she did not choose and cannot use.

The colony died, a mineral bloom replaced it, two hundred and fifty years went and the mind path came back. That subspecies is the only place in the setting where both halves of her symbiosis can be measured against each other, because both halves are in one body — everything the colony did for a lanternfolk and everything it prevented, on a frame where the loss is legible. She has asked twice to go and read it and has been refused twice on the ground that a matcher carrying a conclusion is a matcher whose conclusions arrive with the child.

The prize is whether a body may be entered at all as a person with a life, and it cannot be split because the frame tells her species from the subspecies by whether the fungal organ dies — so a register that separates them is classifying by a temporary organ and one that joins them loses the only difference that predicts what the body can do. She is the living instance of the question and has been described in it, once, as evidence.

Its whole method is to read the dead as the frame said, and the frame says her species differs from the subspecies by an organ that grows, occupies the interior, and can be replaced or lost. That method is why her strain is catalogued and she is not: the register keeps a card for Vellum and no card at all for the hand it lives in, and she has been on every matching list in the deep ground for a hundred and forty years under a word that is not her name.

A single resonator that a sealed population draws qi from, held under a charter and described only by those already answering it — so it reads as an imprint rather than a source, and settling it would need an observation made from outside its own resonance. She lives inside an equivalent arrangement, has never once been able to observe Vellum from outside its own answering, and has read this record four times as the only description of her position that the setting has ever produced.

The cost of exclusion made explicit: a body excluded from a congregation is buried by the congregation that excluded it, and the law requiring it is written down in the excluded party's own name. She has read the provision and cannot apply it to herself, because her strain would be the name written down and it is not hers — which is the cleanest statement of her position she has ever found and the reason she copied it out rather than acted on it.

reference_stats.summary: Cannot fight, cannot bear light, and would not leave a saturated stratum if paid to. What she has is a working knowledge of a living fungal organ that nobody else in the setting holds: two and a half centuries of matching, sixty-one children cleared by her judgement, and the ability to read a colony's answer off wet stone with the flat of one hand. The colony transacts with cave air on its own initiative whether or not she agrees, which makes her the only person alive who can feel what her body is doing without it, and the only person who has decided not to ask it to do more.
strengths: reads a colony's response on stone by touch alone, in the dark, faster than it can be read any other way in the setting

weaknesses: cannot leave saturated air: dry, sunlit or vibrating ground kills the colony within a season and the body goes with it
cannot take the mind path, so the one door her species closed is the one she can never walk back to

reference_stats.combat_read: There is no exchange and she will not attempt one; she is thin, cold, slow and would not last a season on dry ground, which is the most reliable way to kill a lanternfolk and the cheapest. Fire ends one quickly. Anything that is not fire takes a season, which is time enough for her to be somewhere wet. Do not separate her from the saturated ground and do not expect her to answer a charge: she carries no technique that would. The threat to her is administrative — one sentence in a pairing chamber, and it has already been said once.
notes: No figure is quoted for her anywhere, because the register keeps a card for the strain and no card for the holder, and a matcher is counted in punctures rather than in entries.
The eleven punctures down her left forearm are the only complete record of her working life and the only one she has never been asked to produce.

name: Osric Vandel
aliases: the one who said the price out loud

identity.realm: First gate offered, at two hundred and four, and refused in the terms the refusal had to be made in. Never attempted, never held. Nothing anatomical closed this to him: a longmarrow's body path is the one door that will never open, because hardening the marrow stops the turnover its qi depends on, and the qi and mind paths are both complete and both the finest in the record — mind especially, since four centuries of one subject is a discipline no other population has. What closed it is arithmetic he can name in figures. A gate is paid for out of the marrow, and so is a child, and he has four children and no store. He has not held a gate since the refusal and does not expect to hold one he could pay for.

appearance.presentation: A birth attendant of his own kind, which in a household run on attendance is a trade and not a seat, because a man who spends his life in other people's rooms is permanently the least senior person in any of them. He is introduced at a family gathering as a trade rather than as a member, and has been introduced that way for a hundred and forty years, and has never once corrected it.
appearance.age: Four hundred and six. A longmarrow's span is four centuries, so he is six years past the end of a working life by his own arithmetic and the oldest living thing in his household by a margin nobody likes to say aloud. He is also the only member of that household who knows what the end of a longmarrow's span actually costs, because he is the one who has been counting the store since the first child.
appearance.build: Long-boned and light, with dense bone and almost no muscle, narrow at the wrist and long in the forearm — and upright in a way his species is not, because a body that stores rather than moves has never had a reason to develop the stoop of somebody leaning over a surface for four centuries. He stands the way other people stand when they have nothing to lean on.
appearance.complexion: Ivory going grey at the temples, with a cold blue cast across the hands and feet, and the deep translucency at the sternum and the inside of each wrist that the species wears where the store sits.
appearance.hair: Iron grey, cut blunt at the jaw and startlingly thick, because a body that has never stopped replacing a single part of itself in four hundred years has never once thinned at the scalp. It is the most visibly wrong thing about him and it is entirely correct.
appearance.eyes: Pale, deep-set and entirely steady, with an acuity that is not supernatural and is only patiently arrived at — four centuries of pattern recognition arriving late and completely.
appearance.palette: Bone, undyed wool, cold slate-blue, and one warm value: a small dull amber at the sternum where the store is, low and dim. Every saturated colour that appears in any picture of him is on somebody else's wool, and never on his.
appearance.attire: A heavy undyed wool wrap over a plain shift, sleeves pushed back past the elbow and tied there so his forearms stay clear, and a length of belting that he uses at other people's births and has never once needed for his own. Nothing fastened at the throat, and nothing on him that requires a record to say who owns it.
appearance.marks: None. No scars and no cutting anywhere on the body, which is a longmarrow's ordinary condition and which he has noticed, late and without much pleasure, is the reason nobody can read his children off him. His entire count is in his head.
appearance.bearing: Upright, unhurried, and entirely without deference, which in a house whose rule is that whoever is present outranks whoever is absent reads as an error in him rather than as an opinion. He enters a room as though the room has been waiting for him, and he is nearly always right about that.

canon.role_in_story: Every institution this species has ever built is built to put a longmarrow in a room holding something: the Memory keeps its archive in one body because bone that turns over at about a percent a year can neither be edited nor burned by anybody else, and the Seats have no head because a lifespan that outlasts the memory of anybody's predecessors makes authority impossible, so the house runs on attendance and whoever is in the room outranks whoever is not. Osric Vandel is the one member who holds nothing and attends nothing on purpose. A gate is paid for out of the marrow. So is a child — four hundred days of a longmarrow gestation draws on the same tissue the power sits in, and it does not come back on a schedule, because the tissue turns over at about a percent a year and he has four children inside four centuries. He has made that exchange four times and has said so out loud every time, which in a house where the oldest decides nothing and the archive decides for everybody makes him the only person alive who has put a price on anything.
canon.first_appearance: First seen standing — not seated, in a room where four longmarrow of his own family were waiting to be told which of them would hold the next record — answering a question about a child instead of about the record.
canon.lore:
A longmarrow's qi is stored in bone, and bone turns over at roughly a percent a year. That single fact is the species and its whole limitation. It buys four centuries of life and an acuity of pattern no hotter body survives to, and it is why the setting has a durable library at all: a memory held in marrow cannot be edited or burned by anybody else, and it cannot be copied either, so a holder's death is not a copy being retired but the only copy being retired. Nothing in the body's structure refuses a gate — no gate has ever turned a longmarrow away. The limitation is entirely downstream of that success. Turnover is slow, so everything they do is slow, breakthroughs are certain and late, and nothing they have ever built has survived to be inherited intact. That last clause is the whole reason the Memory exists: a library was built to outlive the fact.

What the rest of the setting has not had to price is that a gate is not paid for out of nothing. It is paid for out of the store. A longmarrow's meridian network is seated in the marrow with the soul, which is the deepest and hardest-to-disturb soul in the record and which is also, structurally, the tissue the species reproduces from. So the one organ this population cannot afford to stop replacing is also the one organ everything they are comes out of. A longmarrow who ascends does so by drawing on the reserve; a longmarrow who carries a child does so by drawing on the reserve. The two are the same expenditure, in the same tissue, at rates neither can be scheduled around, because the tissue returns at about a percent a year and a life is four hundred years long.

The species knows this and has never said it. Fertility is near a sixth of a commonborn's, four hundred days of gestation over a four-century span, and the living population is a standing quorum that can never disperse or retire — three centuries of life has not made the line rarer, only slower to replace. Every individual is individually irreplaceable. In a culture that builds its only durable record out of that irreplaceability, a child is the one artefact that carries the species forward, and it is the one artefact nobody has ever put on the list against anything else. Osric has put it on the list. He refused the first gate at two hundred and four, which fixed his arrival order permanently at the back of a house where seniority is a function of attendance, and he has since attended four births, four hundred days each, and has said aloud what each one cost him in a depth of reserve that nobody in that house had been pricing.

And the record will not hold them. The house's rule is that whoever is present outranks whoever is absent, which means a person who spends four centuries being absent from decisions is never overruled and never remembered either. He was never seated in the Memory, by his own choice and by the arithmetic, and his children are therefore not in it either: they will be summarised in whatever summary a house makes when the body that held the detail has gone. There is a place below the spirit peaks where sixty years survive as a summary instead of entry by entry in a culture whose whole practice is that a count is never an estimate, and he has read it four times and drawn the wrong conclusion, which is that a summary is not a failure of record-keeping. It is what a house writes when it is owed four births and refuses to name the debt.
history: Born into a household of eleven living adults and no senior member, which was described to him as the ordinary condition of his species and which he has since understood as a household with no procedure for being finished.
Refused the first gate offered to him at two hundred and four, in the terms the refusal had to be made in, which fixed him last in an arrival order that is the only seniority his house measures.

Took the first of four births at two hundred and sixty-one and said out loud, in front of the whole house, what a child costs the store — a figure no member had been keeping and every member immediately agreed with.

Was asked four times over the following century to take the figure back, on the grounds that the oldest decides nothing and a number spoken aloud is a decision, and refused four times, and was not asked a fifth time.

Carried the fourth child to term at four hundred and six and was not seated in the Memory when the record was made, having declined the appointment on the same arithmetic on which he declined the gate, two hundred years earlier.

He is warm with children and precise with adults and has no interest whatsoever in being liked. What he will not do, under any pressure, is stop keeping the count.

States a number and its year and does not soften either. Repeats a question back when he intends to answer a different one, and never explains that he has done it.

relationships.note: Qi stored in bone that turns over at about a percent a year, so the record is a person and the loss is total. Nothing in the structure refuses a gate and everything is slow. His refusal is not a refusal of that body: it is a decision about which of its two demands to meet, having established that both are drawn from the same marrow and neither is refundable.

The primer teaches qi to take the short route through the long bones, which gives steadier control and better affinity to outside energy and nothing at all that helps a strike land. The long bones are the store. Every hour spent on it is an hour of a technique deliberately driving the reserve through the exact tissue that a longmarrow child is built from, and it is the one discipline in the species he has never once begun.

No head, because a lifespan that outlasts the memory of anyone's predecessors makes authority personal and impossible; governed by attendance, so whoever is present outranks whoever is absent; and owing each generation an hour of presence per period. He has spent two centuries on the far side of that rule, which cost him every decision and gave him his arithmetic, and he has noticed that the rule is also the only thing in the house that cannot be inherited.

The setting's only durable library, held in one body turning over at about a percent a year, so a memory cannot be edited or burned by anybody else — and cannot be copied, so a holder's death is not a copy being retired but the only copy being retired. He declined the appointment, which means his four children are in no record at all and will be summarised when he is gone. That is the price of the four figures he can still give.

The default concentration found in long-settled households, averaged with whatever the house took in, common because it is dependable rather than strong. Three centuries of life has not made this line rarer, only slower to replace. He is the slowest replacement in his household and the only one who has counted what a replacement costs, and both facts come from the same tissue.

The only exact record below the spirit peaks carries sixty years as a summary instead of entry by entry, in a culture whose whole practice is that a count is never an estimate, and compound interest across a gap nobody can fill is what makes the gap matter. He has read it four times and drawn the conclusion the record does not support: that a summary is not a failure of keeping but the shape a house writes when it is owed four births and will not name the debt.

reference_stats.summary: Cannot fight, knows it, and has arranged two centuries so that it cannot matter to him. What he has instead is the only private ledger in the setting: four hundred and six years of one household, one body, and a running figure for what each of four four-hundred-day pregnancies drew out of the store his entire power is seated in. Nothing else in the record can tell you what a longmarrow is worth, because nothing else in the record has spent one and still remembered the price.

reference_stats.combat_read: There is no exchange and he has never trained one. A frame that stores rather than moves has no strike and no way to absorb one, and he would rather be told the price of a fight than be in it. Do not bring force against a man who is light, slow and fragile to a charge: bring a deadline instead. Anything that requires him to be in a room he has made a practice of not being in will work, and the cheapest version of that is simply to schedule a decision on a day he intends to arrive late for.
notes: No figure is quoted for him anywhere, because the house's record is a person and he is not one of the seated, and a man who declined the only office in his species has no entry to be quoted from.
The four figures he can still give are the only written account in the setting of what a longmarrow child costs the body that carries it, and all four are held in a single unwritten head.
